name: Architects and engineering consultancies

problems.words: Clients ask for endless changes and we don't charge for them
quick_ideas: Log every extra request with a rough effort estimate
Raise it with the client before starting the work.

workzap_build.text: A scope-change log with effort estimate, client approval and additional fee, tracked for every project.

problems.ask_first: When a client asks for extra work, what happens?
problems.free_stops: The approval flow and fee link are in the solution document.

problems.words: We have no idea how many hours each project actually takes
quick_ideas: Ask the team to log hours by project for one week
Compare that week against the fee for the largest project.

workzap_build.text: Simple timesheets on phone or web by project and stage, with fee used against budget shown every day.

problems.ask_first: How are timesheets filled in today?
problems.free_stops: Timesheet structure and fee-burn alerts are in the solution document.

problems.words: Stage invoices go out late because nobody tells accounts
quick_ideas: List all stages completed but not yet invoiced
Make marking a stage complete the trigger to tell accounts the same day.

workzap_build.text: A project register where completing a stage raises the invoice task automatically.

problems.ask_first: Who decides a stage is complete?
problems.free_stops: Stage definitions and invoice triggers are in the solution document.

problems.words: Clients pay design fees months late
quick_ideas: Put all unpaid fees in one list by age
Name one person to follow up each week.

workzap_build.text: Fee receivables with ageing and reminders on schedule.

problems.ask_first: How long do clients take to pay?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing and escalation are in the solution document; fee disputes go to a lawyer.

problems.words: Some staff are overloaded while others have little to do
quick_ideas: Map each person's projects for the next few weeks on one page
Review it in a short weekly meeting.

workzap_build.text: A resource planner showing each person's load for the coming weeks, by team.

problems.ask_first: How do you see who has capacity today?
problems.free_stops: Planning rules and views are in the solution document.

problems.words: We issued the wrong drawing revision to site
quick_ideas: Keep one register of current revisions per project
Record every issue to site with date and recipient.

workzap_build.text: A drawing register with revision control and a transmittal log of what went to whom and when.

problems.ask_first: Where are the current drawings kept?
problems.free_stops: Revision rules and transmittal flow are in the solution document.

problems.words: Approval files sit at the authority and we can't track them
quick_ideas: List every submission with date, authority and last comment
Review the oldest ones weekly.

workzap_build.text: An authority approval tracker with submission dates, comments, resubmissions and status for every file.

problems.ask_first: Which authorities do you submit to most?
problems.free_stops: Status stages and alerts are in the solution document.

problems.words: RFIs from the contractor pile up and responses are late
quick_ideas: Log each RFI with date received and owner
Set a response target and check it weekly.

workzap_build.text: An RFI and site-visit log with response deadlines and report templates.

problems.free_stops: Deadlines and report formats are in the solution document.

problems.words: Fee proposals take days and we win few
quick_ideas: Note why each recent proposal was won or lost
Reuse a past proposal as a base for similar projects.

workzap_build.text: A proposal tracker with win/loss reasons and lead source, and a proposal builder drawing on past project data.

problems.ask_first: Where do most new projects come from?
problems.free_stops: Proposal structure and win/loss analysis are in the solution document.

problems.words: Professional registrations and insurance renewals are missed
quick_ideas: Put every registration and insurance expiry in one calendar
Give one person ownership.

workzap_build.text: A renewal calendar with alerts well ahead of every expiry.

problems.ask_first: Who keeps track of expiry dates today?
problems.free_stops: Alert timing is set in the solution document.

never_say: Any opinion on structural adequacy, loads, fire escapes, seismic matters or MEP sizing; that is for the registered engineer. Any help stamping drawings without review, lending a stamp, backdating approvals or paying to speed up a naqsha pass. Any view on professional liability, contracts or fee disputes; suggest legal advice. Any recording of staff salaries, names or personal details. Anything other than emergency services and the authority for an immediate building danger.

sample_reply.person: How do we stop working for free? We charge a lump-sum fee and clients keep adding floors and changing layouts.
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this can be fixed, and you can begin this week. 1 Log every extra request with a rough effort estimate, so the extra work is visible. 2 Raise each one with the client before starting, so the fee conversation happens up front. Workzap can do this automatically for you: a scope-change log with client approval, and timesheets showing fee used against budget on every project. Shall I prepare a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
